findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import time, not per-instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default. Field defaults (unlike `default_factory`) are evaluated exactly once, at class-definition time (i.e. at module import / process startup), and that same datetime object is reused for every `AssignmentSource` instance that doesn't explicitly pass `queued`. This means `AssignmentSource.from_integration(...)` (used on every inbound assignment) always produces the same stale timestamp (process start time) rather than the actual time the assignment was queued. Should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued type is not preserved across serialize/deserialize round trip
findings.body: `to_dict()`/`from_dict()` are used to pass an `AssignmentSource` through a Celery task's kwargs (`sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(..., assignment_source_dict=...)`). The `queued` field is a `datetime` object; once it is serialized to the task broker (JSON) and deserialized on the worker side, `queued` will come back as a string (ISO-formatted) rather than a `datetime`. `from_dict` does not convert it back, so `AssignmentSource.queued` silently becomes a string after the round trip, inconsistent with its declared type and potentially breaking any future code that treats `queued` as a datetime (e.g. arithmetic, timezone comparisons).

findings.title: assignment_source added to sync_status_outbound signature but never wired into loop-prevention logic
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` now accepts an `assignment_source` parameter, mirroring the assignee flow, but unlike `should_sync` for `outbound_assignee`, there is no corresponding check that compares `assignment_source.integration_id` against the target integration for status syncing. This leaves the same inbound/outbound sync-cycle bug this PR is meant to fix still possible for status syncs, and adds a parameter that currently has no behavioral effect (dead parameter) unless callers and subclasses are updated to actually use it.

findings.title: No test exercises assignment_source_dict through an actual serialized Celery round trip
findings.body: All new tests call `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign` and rely on `self.tasks()` to execute the dispatched task in-process, which keeps the `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` output as native Python objects (including a real `datetime` for `queued`). There is no test that serializes the task kwargs through an actual message broker/JSON encoder, so the datetime round-trip inconsistency described above (queued becoming a string after real serialization) is not caught by the test suite.

findings.title: Typo in test method name
findings.body: `test_from_dict_inalid_data` should be `test_from_dict_invalid_data`. Minor, but reduces discoverability/readability of the test and indicates it wasn't proofread.
